rounds.text: Significant structural risks and insider divestment cloud the investment case for Thomas Scott India Ltd. Promoters have sharply reduced their stake from 69.64% in September 2023 down to 52.32% by June 2026, marking a substantial 17.32 percentage point dilution in insider commitment [E1]. This promoter exodus is mirrored by foreign institutional investors slashing their holdings to a negligible 0.04% alongside negative institutional money flow signals [E2, E4]. Operationally, the business carries extreme downside volatility, evidenced by a staggering historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -88.7% and an annualized volatility rate of 61.7% [E10, E11]. Furthermore, a major accident at the Bhiwandi warehouse resulted in the catastrophic loss of fixed assets and an inventory carrying value of approximately Rs. 21.85 crores [E33, E34]. Conceded: the company maintains solid technical momentum trading above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside encouraging near-term demand commentary [E7, E26]. Nevertheless, sector fundamentals remain uninspiring with a modest median ROCE of just 7.6% [E23].
